bookFraming.commercialTagsPlaceholder: For example: comeback, strong conflict, high suspense, workplace maneuvering
bookFraming.competingFeelPlaceholder: For example: a realistic workplace sense of pressure with a touch of dry humor and dense relationship tension
bookFraming.description: In the plainest words, spell out who this book is for, what its selling points are, and what readers get in the first 30 chapters. It is fine if you cannot write professional pitch copy; just describe it by instinct.
bookFraming.first30PromisePlaceholder: For example: the first 30 chapters must let readers see the protagonist secure a first-stage footing, the core rival surface, the relationship line hit its first strong reversal, and make it clear the book only gets more intense from there.
bookFraming.sellingPointLabel: Core selling point of this book
bookFraming.sellingPointPlaceholder: For example: every time the protagonist solves a real predicament, it leverages a bigger web of relationships and interests, so readers keep anticipating the next pushback.
bookFraming.targetAudiencePlaceholder: For example: readers who love urban high-pressure comebacks, relationship tension, and constant page-turning hooks

titleQuickFill.appliedLibrary: The library title was written into the creation form.

titleQuickFill.briefNote: This only affects this one generation and is not written back to the novel creation form.

worldDialog.assetHint.characterNetwork: Once faction affiliations and faction pressures are filled in, character relationships fit the world better.
worldDialog.assetHint.default: Fill in the world handbook first, then organize the visual assets.
worldDialog.assetHint.factionDiagram: Once the main forces, goals, and pressures are filled in, the diagram can show faction relationships.
worldDialog.assetHint.map: Once the story stages and location risks are filled in, the map can show regions and conflict flashpoints.
worldDialog.assetHint.powerSystemTree: Once core rules, costs, and boundaries are filled in, the system tree avoids becoming a mere ranking table.
worldDialog.assetHint.timeline: Once the core conflicts and shared consequences are filled in, the timeline can show how the situation shifts.
worldDialog.assets.description: Maps, faction diagrams, timelines, and system trees help you see the world; they are not the sole source for chapter generation.
worldDialog.assets.empty: The world-asset entry points are organized together with the book's world handbook.
worldDialog.assets.title: World assets
worldDialog.dialogDescription: View the book's world handbook, generation constraints, and usage scope. This content serves character, outline, and chapter generation.
worldDialog.guidance.description: These explain how the book's world enters character, outline, and chapter generation.
worldDialog.guidance.title: Generation constraints
worldDialog.overview.description: This shows the headline info for the book's world to help you judge whether it supports the current story.
worldDialog.overview.summaryFallback: This book's world is still being prepared.
worldDialog.overview.title: World overview
worldDialog.rules.description: Chapter generation prioritizes these hard rules to avoid inventing inconsistent settings on the fly.
worldDialog.rules.tensionsDescription: These long-term conflicts help the outline and chapters keep the world's pressure.
worldDialog.rules.title: Rules and costs
worldDialog.source.chooseDescription: Import from the world library, generate for this book, or create a custom world skeleton first.
worldDialog.source.chooseTitle: Choose or change the book's world source
worldDialog.source.description: Import from the world library, generate for this book, or save the book's world as a reusable sample.
worldDialog.source.saveToLibraryDesc: Save the book's world as a reusable sample; later you can push this book's changes or pull library content.
worldDialog.source.title: Source and world library
worldDialog.sync.cannotSync: Sync is not available right now.
worldDialog.sync.description: First see where the book's world differs from the library sample, then choose the sections to sync. The system never overwrites either side automatically.
worldDialog.sync.diffOnOpen: The difference summary is read when you open the book's world.
worldDialog.sync.historyDescription: View the last few manual sync records.
worldDialog.sync.inSync: The book's world matches the library sample.
worldDialog.sync.independentNote: The book's world is used as an independent copy. When you need to sync, you can manually push the book's world or pull the library content.
worldDialog.sync.manualHint: Pushing changes the library sample; pulling changes the book's world copy.
worldDialog.sync.selectSectionHint: Only sync the overview, rules, forces, locations, or relationship network you have confirmed.
worldDialog.sync.title: Sync management
worldDialog.syncDirection.pull: Pull from the world library only
worldDialog.syncDirection.push: Push to the world library only
worldSource.chooseDescription: First decide where this novel's world comes from, then expand the matching action. Every path creates the book's own world copy.
worldSource.generate.choiceDescription: Best when you have no clear world setting yet; let the system generate the book's world from the title, overview, selling points, and type.
worldSource.generate.panelDescription: The system generates a world for the book from the title, overview, selling points, reader promise, and type. Good for quickly forming a usable stage when starting a new book.
worldSource.generate.panelTitle: Generate a world for this book
worldSource.generate.saveToLibraryNote: Save to the world library after generating so other novels can reuse it.
worldSource.generate.title: Generate for this book
worldSource.import.choiceDescription: Best when you already have a reusable world sample; copy one as the book's world and decide whether to sync manually.
worldSource.import.keepSyncNote: Keep the sync entry after importing. The system only flags differences and never overwrites the book's world or the library sample automatically.
worldSource.import.panelDescription: Importing copies the external world handbook. The book uses this copy during generation, and the external world library is not changed automatically.
worldSource.import.title: Import from sample library
worldSource.manual.choiceDescription: Best when you have a clear idea; create the book's world skeleton first, then gradually fill in rules, forces, and locations.
worldSource.manual.panelDescription: Create a blank world handbook first, then flesh out the core rules, main forces, story stages, and key tensions in the world workspace.
worldSource.manual.summaryPlaceholder: For example: a border empire whose star-core is depleting, where magic and power both come at a cost.
worldSource.manual.title: Custom blank handbook
